legend.purpose: Uppercase label of a field or select.

tag.purpose: The classification at the start of a status sentence.

shadows.name: none

shadows.purpose: Outline of the quiet key. The ghost key uses the same ring in white on the band.

shadows.name: ring-chip
shadows.purpose: Outline of a chip on white; on-soft on the band, 2px white on band hover and focus.

shadows.name: ring-unread
shadows.purpose: A cell the lookup never reached.

shadows.name: ring-loupe-aim
shadows.purpose: The centre cell of the loupe.

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Focus everywhere (an outline, not a shadow). Offset 2px on fields and code blocks; white inside the band and the footer.

motion.name: out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--out), for every animation of a bit being read or written.

motion.name: land
motion.purpose: One of the seven cells arriving.

motion.name: probe-interval
motion.value: 150ms between cells, then 180ms before the verdict
motion.purpose: The seven cells fill in order and stop at the first 0.

motion.name: drop
motion.purpose: A mark landing on the bit picture.

motion.name: mark-hot
motion.purpose: A mark while its cell is pointed at.

motion.name: flip
motion.value: 480ms var(--out) backwards; from scale(0.4) on mark yellow with ink text; 70ms stagger

motion.name: pending
motion.purpose: The previous verdict and reason while the cells are still filling.

motion.name: key
motion.purpose: Key hover and press. Chips use the same 120ms background change.

motion.name: status-clear
motion.purpose: How long the copy status text stays.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none; transition: none; scroll-behavior: auto
motion.purpose: With prefers-reduced-motion the answer appears complete and the run is drawn in one step.

bitPicture.order: row by row, bit 0 at the top left
bitPicture.pixels: one canvas pixel per device pixel, at most two per bit; each is the area-weighted mix of --on and --off

narrative.overview:
A Bloom filter is a row of bits, so the site draws bits and nothing that needs explaining first. The unit is one square cell holding a monospace 0 or 1: pale when it is 0, solid cobalt when it is 1. The same unit appears at every scale: three to five cells above a rule, seven cells for an answer, an eight by eight grid, a seven by seven loupe, a hundred by hundred run of squares, and one picture of all 1,657,884 bits where each cell has shrunk to a dot.

The page is white with navy ink and one cobalt. A single full-width cobalt band holds the 64-bit grid, the install section sits on a pale tint, and the footer is navy. Everything is flat. Type is a heavy condensed sans for headings and verdicts, its regular-width sibling for sentences, and the platform monospace for anything a machine holds or a visitor types. Recorded from the shipped `docs/site/style.css`, `app.js`, `field.js` and `assets/social-card.html`. This replaces the punched-card system, which is retired.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, navy ink, one cobalt. Cobalt means a 1.
One unit, the cell: a square with a 4px radius holding a monospace 0 or 1.
The real filter is one picture of every bit in a pale frame, painted from the real snapshot.
A yellow disc with a navy edge marks a bit a key points at.
One cobalt band per page; inside it the cell inverts and a 1 is white.
Flat: no cast shadows, no gradients, no textures, no card containers.
Brand marks are the real files. Nothing is drawn or generated to stand in for one.

rules.name: The One Cobalt Rule
rules.body: There is one accent hue. Cobalt means a 1, and by extension the thing to press and the answer "probably". No second accent, no status green or red: a "no" is navy ink, not a colour.

rules.name: The Pointing Rule
rules.body: `mark` means "a key points here". It appears as the numbered disc, the aim ring, the flip, and the text selection, and nowhere else. It always sits beside navy and is always backed by text (the numeral on the disc, the status sentence, the address under the cell).

rules.name: The Inverted Band Rule
rules.body: Inside the cobalt band the cell inverts: a 1 is white with a cobalt numeral, a 0 is `on-deep` with an `on-soft` numeral. Secondary text is `on-soft`, focus outlines are white, tags are white with ink text.

rules.name: The Three Faces Rule
rules.body: Condensed is for headings, verdicts, keys, legends and tags. Barlow is for sentences. Monospace is for bits, bit addresses, typed keys, chips and code, and never for a sentence.

rules.name: The Legend Rule
rules.body: An uppercase legend labels a control. It never sits above a heading as a category line.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No offset, no blur, no gradient, no texture. Separate with a ground change, a 2px ink rule, or a 1px `off-edge` hairline. A ring drawn with `box-shadow` must have zero offset and zero blur.

dos: Do draw any new state as cells: `off` for 0, `on` for 1, square, 4px radius, monospace numeral.
Do keep text on white, `tint`, the band or the navy footer, with the pairs measured above.
Do give every yellow mark a navy edge and a text equivalent.
Do invert cells, tags, keys and focus outlines inside the band.
Do separate with a ground change, a 2px ink rule or a 1px `off-edge` hairline.
Do paint pictures of bits from the real snapshot, one canvas pixel per device pixel, with colours read from the custom properties.

Do use the real brand files: `docs/site/assets/mill5-logo.png`, `docs/site/assets/richard-crane.jpg`, and the NuGet package icon `M5.BloomFilter/bitarray_400-min.png` (shipped as `icon-64.png` and `icon-180.png`).
Do render `social-card.png` from `assets/social-card.html` whenever the headline or figures change.
donts: Don't draw, generate, trace or approximate a logo, mark, portrait or icon. If an asset is missing, ask for the file.
Don't bring back the punched cards, the fan-fold paper, or any other metaphor that has to be explained before the filter is.
Don't add a second accent hue, or use `mark` for emphasis, links, buttons, backgrounds or text.
Don't add a second cobalt band, or a second tinted section, to a page.
Don't add a cast shadow, blur, gradient or texture, or box a section as a card.
Don't introduce another radius, or a cell that is not square.
Don't set sentences in monospace or in uppercase condensed, and don't put a legend above a heading.
Don't set text in `off-edge`, `off` or `mark`, or soft ink on the band.
Don't load fonts, scripts or images from another origin.
